methodology: Historical player-round outcomes are forecast using only previous observed player-rounds and lagged CR. Candidate lineups use each player’s latest observed CR/role/team strictly before the target round; prices are carried forward if the player had no row in the immediately prior round. Opponent features use reconstructed high-confidence target dates and NBA team statistics strictly before the target date. Coach base-score outcomes are reconstructed from final NBA team scores/margin/OT with equal coach CR so the price-difference coefficient is neutral.
limitations: Historical credit is the last observed prior-round CR, carried forward for players with no appearance row in the immediately prior round; the archived tables are not full timestamped market snapshots.

The candidate universe contains players who have appeared earlier in the season; it misses players not yet observed in the archive. It covers on average about 94.9% of players listed in the target-round outcomes, but this is not the same as proving full market coverage.
Historical coach CR and opponent coach CR are missing. Coach outcomes are reconstructed with equal prices, so coach selection/price-difference multiplier and exact coach PDK are not validated.

Lineup experiment uses no transfer malus because historical carried rosters are not archived. The model-versus-baseline result is a fresh-lineup proxy comparison, not a complete transfer-policy backtest.
Target-round date mapping uses high-consensus official player/game identity matching to infer the schedule date; target PDK is used only for linkage, never as a model feature.

Seasons 2018/19 and 2019/20 remain excluded from supervised player-score targets where the official Dunkest validity flag is false; NBA results from those years can still train the reconstructed coach base-score model.
